subject: Request: one-time onboarding credit + custom invoice cadence for ACME Retail
messages:
From: Jenna Park <procurement@acmeretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request for onboarding credit + accelerated invoicing cadence

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. ACME is excited about Redwood — the latency and cost story aligns well with our Q1 roadmap. Procurement and finance asked me to confirm whether Redwood can: (1) provide a one-time onboarding credit against the first quarter invoice; and (2) accept an accelerated invoice cadence (net 30 on the first two draws, then monthly) to align with our internal chargebacks.

We are evaluating a 12-month committed usage agreement with a $1.2M ARR run rate and can agree to an upfront 50% commit if we get clarity on credits and the payment cadence. In short, two asks: a 20–30% one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) and the custom invoice cadence above.

I’ve attached our committed usage schedule and the term sheet with our preferred billing language. Can you route this for internal sign-off? Procurement would like a yes/no by end of week.

Thanks,
Jenna Park
Procurement Manager, ACME Retail
procurement@acmeretail.com

Attachments: acme_committed_usage_schedule.xlsx, term_sheet_v2_redlines.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request for onboarding credit + accelerated invoicing cadence

Monica / Marissa — forwarding ACME’s request. Quick summary:
- ACME wants a 12-month, $1.2M ARR committed deal with 50% upfront commitment.
- Asks: 20–30% one-time onboarding credit; modified invoice cadence (net 30 on first two draws).
- They sign early if we can confirm credit and cadence this week.

Attached their schedule + redlines. My rough margin calc: with the commit and 50% up-front, unit economics look OK at 25% credit if we hold to a 12-month locked rate. But the accelerated invoice cadence increases our DSOs on the first two invoices — need finance confirmation on cash flow impact.

Proposed options:
1) Approve 25% onboarding credit, require 50% upfront payment to mitigate DSO.
2) Approve 15% credit with standard net-45 invoicing.
3) Decline credit and offer a one-time professional services discount instead (smaller margin hit).

Can you review and advise. If we proceed with #1 we’ll need VP/CFO signoff for anything >20% per policy. I created a short draft memo attached (one-page-credit-memo.docx) that you can sign off.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_committed_usage_schedule.xlsx, term_sheet_v2_redlines.pdf, one-page-credit-memo.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for onboarding credit + accelerated invoicing cadence

Thanks Karthik — reviewed the numbers. A few points:
- With 50% upfront on $1.2M ARR (i.e., $600k) our cash exposure reduces materially, so a larger one-time credit is defensible.
- Margin sensitivity: a 25% onboarding credit on the first quarter (approx $75–90k) is acceptable if we lock the 12-month rate and require the 50% upfront.
- The modified cadence (net 30 x2) is fine operationally if Finance records the first two invoices as restricted receivables; we should avoid prepaid revenue recognition issues.

Requesting Marissa to produce an exception memo for >20% credits and a recommendation to route to VP/CFO for final sign-off. If approved, Sales should confirm the exact invoice schedule in the master term sheet and add a clause limiting the one-time credit to onboarding services only (not ongoing usage).

Also tagging an ask: can we cap the effective lifetime discount by including a clause that disallows stacking with future promotional credits? Keeps long-term unit economics intact.

-Monica
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Park <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for onboarding credit + accelerated invoicing cadence — exception memo

Team — I reviewed the deal economics and drafted an exception memo below for VP/CFO review. I recommend approving a one-time onboarding credit at 25% applied to the first invoice only, contingent on the following:

- Financial mitigations: 50% upfront payment of the annual committed amount to be received within 14 days of contract signing. Remaining first-quarter invoice due net-30 after the upfront draw.
- Contract conditions: 12-month committed usage at the locked rate; credit applied only to onboarding professional services (itemized in SOW). No stacking with future promotional discounts; credit void if customer terminates before 6 months.
- Operational: Finance to treat first two invoices as restricted receivables and confirm AR workflow before sending terms to customer.

Memo (one-line): Approve one-time onboarding credit of 25% for ACME Retail on a 12-month, $1.2M ARR commit, conditioned on 50% upfront payment and the contract safeguards above.

Please consider this my recommendation for an exception. If leadership concurs, route to CFO for final signoff and send the redlined term sheet back to Jenna.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
VP, Finance (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: one-page-credit-memo.docx

From: Jenna Park <procurement@acmeretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request for onboarding credit + accelerated invoicing cadence

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround. ACME accepts the proposed conditions: 25% onboarding credit applied to onboarding services only, 50% upfront payment within 14 days, and the invoice cadence as described. We’ll proceed with signature once you provide the final redlines.

Jenna Park
Procurement Manager, ACME Retail
procurement@acmeretail.com
